chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding a nose of the slave, or his manhood, or something which overcame his value, that he has to pay to his master the value of the slave, and take the slave.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on compensating for injury to a slave's body parts?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of 'diya al-kamilah' (full compensation) for significant injuries to a slave, where the injurer pays the slave's total market value to the master and assumes ownership. This mechanism effectively transfers the slave from the master to the injurer, serving as both restitution and a form of corporal punishment or debt settlement. It highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence on property rights and bodily integrity within the social hierarchy of the time.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a nose of the slave, or his manhood, or something which overcame his value, and he has to pay to his master the value of the slave, and take the slave’.
